title: Relational data modelling
brief: Design rows, keys and relationships that express the shop’s facts accurately. Diagnose dependencies and redundancy, distinguish historical facts from derived copies, and judge normalisation and modelling variations through required changes.

neighbouring_ownership.normalisation: Owns precise formal definitions, closure and decomposition methods.
neighbouring_ownership.hierarchies: Owns hierarchy representation comparisons and working maintenance procedures.
neighbouring_ownership.constraints: Owns enforcement, including subtype completeness and tenant references.
neighbouring_ownership.history: Owns temporal procedures; modelling establishes the difference between current and agreed price.

title: Constraints and data integrity
brief: Express identity, required values, row checks, references and exclusions in enforceable schema rules. Preserve tenant integrity with composite identities and references, and distinguish declarative enforcement, triggers and invariants needing a concurrency protocol.

neighbouring_ownership.access-control: Owns who may read or change rows.
neighbouring_ownership.transactions: Owns concurrent protocols for rules beyond declarative constraints.
neighbouring_ownership.history: Owns correction and deletion policy; constraints applies that policy to references.

title: Joins and the meaning of a result row
brief: Build SELECT and JOIN results with deliberate row meaning. Predict multiplicity and missing matches, use existence tests, distinguish compatible-row set operations and their duplicates from joining columns, and complete the still-due report by summarising lines and payments separately per order.

neighbouring_ownership.aggregation: Owns general grouping, HAVING, FILTER, empty/count distinctions and windows; query results owns only the narrow per-order GROUP BY/SUM summary required for its report.
neighbouring_ownership.query-execution: Owns physical join methods and execution order.

ownership_note: Own compact UNION ALL/UNION duplicate semantics and orientation to INTERSECT/EXCEPT; no separate thin child.
